resources.string: MotoMesh — open-source OrangLoRa mesh voice chat for motorcyclists.
VOX delay, ducking threshold, and noise gate controls — coming in a future update.
Only riders on the same channel can hear each other
Sensitivity: %1$d (higher = louder voice required to duck music)
Music volume drops to %1$d%% when voice detected
No riders yet.\nTap Connect to start, or open Settings to configure the transport.
Loopback mode — mic to speakers.\nUnmute and speak to hear yourself.

1. Pair RYLR993 in Bluetooth (passkey: 123456)
2. Tap Connect → choose your module
3. Wait for Connected status
4. Other riders on this channel appear here
1. Set relay host & port in Settings → Network\n2. Tap Connect\n3. Other riders on the same relay appear here
Your microphone feeds directly to your headphones. No network, no hardware needed. Use this to test audio quality and latency.

Requires a RYLR993 LoRa module paired via Bluetooth.

1. Power the module via USB (use a 3.3V regulator)
2. Pair in Android Bluetooth: Settings → Bluetooth → scan for "RYLR993_XXXX"
3. Passkey: 123456
4. In MotoMesh, tap Connect → pick your module
5. Repeat on each rider's phone
6. All riders on the same channel will be visible here.

No hardware needed. Uses a TCP relay server.

1. Run relay_server.py on any computer: python3 relay_server.py
2. Note the IP address of that computer
3. In MotoMesh Settings → Network, enter the IP and port (default 60005)
4. Tap Connect — audio is relayed through the server to other riders.
Set a channel (0-15) in Settings → Network.\nOnly riders on the same channel can hear each other.\nUse different channels for different ride groups.
Three ways to connect. Choose what fits your ride.
Tap the LOOPBACK badge above to cycle: Loopback (no network) → LoRa (radio) → Cellular (TCP relay). Each mode shows different instructions below.
In Android Bluetooth Settings → Pair new device. Look for "RYLR993_XXXX". Passkey is 123456. The app auto-configures everything on connect.
Open Settings → Network. Enter the relay server\'s IP address and port. Run relay_server.py on any computer on the same network.
No setup needed. Tap the mic icon to unmute. Your voice goes mic → headphones. Great for testing.
The big green button. In LoRa mode it scans for nearby modules. In Cellular mode it dials the relay server. Watch the status bar turn green when connected.
Each rider on your network/channel appears as a card. Tap a rider to see RSSI, loss rate, and last heard time. The notification shows how many riders are online.
Open Settings → Audio. Drag VOX threshold higher if music ducks too easily. Drag Duck depth shallower if the volume drop is too harsh. Changes apply instantly.
In Settings → Network, set a Channel number (0-15). Only riders on the same channel hear each other. Great for splitting ride groups.
Your callsign is visible to all riders in the mesh.
Callsign must be 20 characters or fewer.
